usage:
require "openai"

client = Openai::Client.new(api_key: ENV["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

result = client.vector_stores.create(file_ids: ["string"], name: "string", description: "string", expires_after: { "anchor" => "last_active_at", "days" => 1 }, chunking_strategy: { "type" => "auto" }, metadata: { "key" => "string" })
pp result

typeReference.signature: client.vector_stores.create(file_ids: nil, name: nil, description: nil, expires_after: nil, chunking_strategy: nil, metadata: nil) -> Models::VectorStoreObject

fields.name: file_ids
fields.description: A list of [File](/docs/api-reference/files) IDs that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the vector store.

fields.name: description
fields.description: A description for the vector store. Can be used to describe the vector store's purpose.

fields.name: chunking_strategy
fields.description: The chunking strategy used to chunk the file(s). If not set, will use the `auto` strategy. Only applicable if `file_ids` is non-empty.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

fields.name: object
fields.description: The object type, which is always `vector_store`.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the vector store was created.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the vector store.

fields.name: usage_bytes
fields.description: The total number of bytes used by the files in the vector store.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the vector store, which can be either `expired`, `in_progress`, or `completed`. A status of `completed` indicates that the vector store is ready for use.
